caveats: The chart compares annual median reported owner discretionary earnings with annual median sales for nationally reported sold businesses. A ratio of medians is not the median of individual-business margins.

Seller’s discretionary earnings (SDE) can add back one owner’s compensation and benefits, interest, depreciation, amortization and selected discretionary or nonrecurring expenses. These ratios are not net profit after replacing a working owner with a manager.

These are national reported sold-business samples, not measured Lewiston margins or a census of all operating firms. Selection, survival, seller reporting and unverified add-backs limit comparability.
Convenience stores exclude gas station listings. Cleaning businesses and laundromats have different service mixes and owner workloads.

A higher SDE ratio does not establish higher annual dollar profit, lower investment, or greater return on capital. Replacement management, ongoing capital expenditure and debt service must be assessed separately.

Pet grooming in 2025 is plotted at 24.5%, calculated as $93,105 / $380,000 × 100. The source table prints 26.0%, which is inconsistent with those two reported medians. All other plotted percentages retain the published rounded values.

metricDefinitions.name: Reported earnings ratio
metricDefinitions.definition: Reported annual median seller discretionary earnings divided by reported annual median revenue, expressed as a percentage.

evidenceFlow.title: Pet grooming arithmetic correction
evidenceFlow.detail: The source reports 2025 median revenue of $380,000 and median SDE of $93,105. Their ratio is 24.5%, not the printed 26.0%. The chart uses the computed ratio; source values are preserved in the supporting research file.
